A day in the life of a milling operator
A milling operator works in a machining workshop. They cut the part on the drawing out of a metal block by removing chips.
The day starts with the work order and technical drawing: the part's dimensions, tolerances and material are read.
The part is clamped in the vice, a suitable milling cutter is fitted, and the spindle speed and feed are set.
The rotating cutter removes thin chips from the part: surfaces are faced, slots and pockets are cut, gears are cut.
When finished, the part is measured with callipers, a micrometer and a dial indicator. If a dimension is outside the tolerance, the part is scrap.
It's learned in the machine technology field of vocational high schools or on courses. Some machining jobs in Türkiye require a vocational qualification certificate.
